# SPY Weekly-Strategy Study ($25/week variations, 2005–2024)

*SPY only · long-only · **every scheme contributes the same $25/week ($1,300/yr)** so we isolate strategy, not dollars. Baseline = $25/wk bought Mondays, always.*

**Baseline (WA1):** $106,735, IRR **12.58%**, max DD -38.10%.

> Note: in the earlier study $25/wk looked like the 'winner' only because it put in $1,300/yr vs $1,200/yr elsewhere — on IRR it was tied. Here everything is $1,300/yr, apples to apples.

## Verdict

1. **Day-of-week timing is noise.** Monday/Wed/Friday land within a couple hundredths of a percent; even buying the week's *cheapest* day with perfect hindsight (WA4) only makes 12.67% = **+0.09%** over Monday. The theoretical ceiling on weekly timing is basically zero.
2. **Weekly vs monthly at equal dollars is a tie** — WE2 ($108.33/mo) ≈ WA1 ($25/wk); frequency doesn't matter.
3. **Same story as before:** the only levers that move anything are the trend filter + cash yield (shave drawdown at ~flat return) — not contribution timing. Nothing here clears +1% IRR.

**Conclusion:** there is no $25/week timing trick that adds ~1%. To out-earn the baseline you must contribute more dollars (as the original $1,300/yr did) — a bigger contribution, not a smarter one.
